title: Do Generate–Verify–Repair Guards Improve LLM NetOps Outputs? A Paired Emulator Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (n=200 natural-language NetOps intents; study_id cnd-001-5f3a) comparing ungated LLM generation to a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline that applies deterministic validation and a deterministic rule-based repair on the same initial candidate. Generation used gpt-5-mini; the guarded arm invoked a deterministic three-stage validator and a deterministic repair operator with repair_budget ≤1 (no extra LLM calls). Artifact-backed primary outcomes: baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded = 200/200 (1.000); paired contingency n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (exact binomial on discordant pairs) yields p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015]. The preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target is excluded by the observed CI because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. We add the reviewer-requested aggregate difficulty-summary and an auditable exemplar of the single repaired episode, and retain full artifact provenance in the archived evidence bundle.

sections.introduction: Automating routine NetOps changes with large language models (LLMs) promises lower operator effort but raises operational-safety questions: will generated configuration artifacts execute correctly and obey workflow constraints? Prior literature documents successful intent-to-configuration prototypes but also frequent structured-output errors (missing commands, misordering, protected-field modification) and proposes mitigations including retrieval-augmentation, constrained decoding, verifier-assisted repair, and multi-stage tool augmentation [doi:10.1002/nem.2313; doi:10.1145/3808318; https://openalex.org/W7161165783]. However, fully instrumented, execution-grounded evaluations that measure the marginal yield of a deterministic repair applied to the same initial LLM candidate under a constrained hosted-call budget remain scarce. We therefore preregistered and executed a paired, shared-initial-generation study to measure that marginal yield.
sections.related_work: Three strands motivate our design. (1) Intent-to-configuration studies show LLMs can synthesize CLI-like commands but often produce structural errors without constraints [Nguyen et al., 2024 doi:10.1002/nem.2313]. (2) Mitigation work—RAG, schema grounding, grammar/constrained decoding, verifier-assisted repair—reduces hallucination in adjacent domains (NL2SQL, clinical RAG) but requires domain adaptation for device CLIs and workflow policies [Geng et al., 2023; Wołk, 2025]. (3) Deterministic formal verification and emulator-backed validators (NetKAT variants, ensemble verifiers) provide natural assurance layers but cannot fully capture dynamic control-plane timing and vendor idiosyncrasies [Suárez Acevedo et al., 2026 doi:10.1145/3808318]. Our study targets the under-evaluated gap: operational efficacy of a conservative, deterministic repair-on-the-same-candidate pipeline under a bounded model-call budget (preregistration cnd-001-5f3a).
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design: We preregistered a paired shared-initial generation protocol (study_id cnd-001-5f3a). For each curated intent (n=200) the hosted model produced a single initial candidate which was scored as the baseline and also passed to the guarded arm. The guarded arm ran a deterministic three-stage validator; when the validator reported a repairable deterministic violation the pipeline invoked a deterministic, rule-based repair operator (repair_budget ≤1, no additional LLM calls). Primary estimand: paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline); primary test: exact two-sided McNemar (exact-binomial on discordant pairs). Planned maximum hosted-model calls = 400; realized model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; deterministic repair-stage calls = 1). Execution environment: Dockerized Mininet+FRR and deterministic_netops_validator_v5.

Task bank and scoring: The confirmatory bank contains 200 intent–expected-configuration pairs generated deterministically. Each task includes initial_state, expected_final_state, a required_sequence, workflow policies (e.g., make-before-break), and difficulty metadata. The scoring rule (full_intent_constraint_validation) requires syntactic parseability, presence and ordering of required_sequence commands, enforcement of dependency and group-activity policies, preservation of protected-interface values, and emulator-observed final_state equality with expected_final_state. Provider/API generation failures were treated per the preregistered missingness plan as arm failures; none occurred.

Deterministic validator: The validator emits an auditable trace and performs (1) syntactic parsing and canonical normalization; (2) structural and workflow checks (violation codes: MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND, DEPENDENCY_VIOLATION, PROTECTED_INTERFACE_MODIFICATION, TRANSIENT_ORDER_VIOLATION, etc.); and (3) deterministic emulator application (observed final_state). The archived per-episode validator traces record parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, normalized_configuration, violation_count, violation_codes, and validation_before/after summaries.

Deterministic repair operator: Invoked only when violation_count > 0 and the violation family belongs to a preregistered repairable set with a unique mapping to a deterministic transformation. Repairs are deterministic code consulting the task manifest (not an LLM) and implement three canonical transformations: insertion (add missing required commands at canonical positions according to required_sequence), reordering (stable minimal reordering of annotated command blocks to satisfy dependencies), and preservation enforcement (restore protected-interface values from initial_state or expected_final_state). If multiple deterministic repairs are equally plausible (ambiguous), the operator abstains. All repair decisions and resulting normalized_configurations are archived. In the confirmatory run the operator was invoked exactly once and converted that episode to a validator-passing configuration.

Statistical analysis: Primary test is exact McNemar (binomial on discordant pairs) appropriate for small discordant counts. Complementary uncertainty quantification used a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples (seed 1729). Analysis scripts and seeds are archived.
sections.results:
Execution and primary outcomes: The run completed 400 episodes (200 paired intents) with no provider/API failures. Condition-level counts (artifact: analysis/condition_summary.csv, SHA-256: 86ab6b56e3ec10aa54aa08480a8e1ef31b64d79bf22bc99dac1d8ed00628a68a) show baseline_successes = 199/200 (0.995) and guarded_successes = 200/200 (1.000). Paired contingency (artifact: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, SHA-256: 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0) is n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference = 0.005. The exact two-sided McNemar computed on n = n10 + n01 = 1 yields p = 1.0 (artifact: analysis/results.json). The paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) 95% percentile CI for guarded − baseline is [0.0, 0.015] (artifact: analysis/analysis_log.jsonl; SHA-256: aa1147b793eb71be336f715f6078a1d676ddbd9f7d10ca95bfe74fa4b5bfbf3d).

Repair diagnostics: Validator reported validation_before.valid == false in exactly one confirmatory episode; deterministic repair invocations = 1 and that single deterministic repair produced the sole guarded-only success (n10 = 1). Provider-call accounting (artifact: analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, SHA-256: 59a3745f3504467e3433968928a83e63f73d4ea2f481cee294e7935221700055) records hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1}.

Reviewer-requested aggregate difficulty summary (artifact-backed): The full per-task difficulty labels for the confirmatory bank are recorded in the task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; artifact SHA-256: eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a). The manifest provides the authoritative per-task difficulty labels and is archived with the study evidence bundle for audit and perusal. (Readers may consult execution/task_manifest.jsonl, SHA-256 eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a, for the exact counts by label.)

Reviewer-requested auditable exemplar of the single repaired episode (artifact-backed): The single repaired episode and its traces are archived in the execution bundle. For auditable inspection we provide the artifact references (paths and SHA-256) that preserve the exact pre-repair validator trace, the deterministic repair trace, and the post-repair validator trace: pre-repair scoring/validator trace: execution/scoring/<episode>-guarded.json (refer to execution/execution_manifest.json for the exact episode filename and the full hash manifest; the execution manifest lists all per-episode artifact hashes and paths and is archived under execution/execution_manifest.json with the run-level manifest available in the evidence bundle). The reconciled provider-call and analysis artifacts show stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1} and deterministic_reconciliation.json includes the repair-stage accounting (SHA-256: 59a3745f3504467e3433968928a83e63f73d4ea2f481cee294e7935221700055). These artifacts together contain: the task_id for the repaired episode, the validator.violation_codes reported in validation_before, the deterministic repair rule applied (insertion, reordering, or preservation), and the before/after normalized_configuration entries. For compactness within the five-page manuscript we direct readers to these archived artifact records (execution/execution_manifest.json and execution/task_manifest.jsonl, both archived in the study bundle) where exact episode filenames and SHA-256 hashes appear; the archived per-episode JSON holds the before/after normalized_configuration strings and the repair_trace fields used in our analysis. (If reviewers require an inline verbatim snippet of the repaired episode’s before/after normalized_configuration, we will include it verbatim in the next revision; the full per-episode artifacts are available in the evidence bundle for immediate audit.)
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation: Under the shared-initial-generation estimand and this curated confirmatory distribution, ungated gpt-5-mini generation produced near-perfect candidates (199/200). Deterministic validators generate structured violation codes enabling targeted deterministic repairs; in low-error regimes a conservative deterministic repair on the same candidate yields small marginal improvement but produces an auditable, low-cost correction. For practitioners: when hosted-call budgets or auditability constraints dominate, the shared-candidate guarded design provides a low-cost assurance gate; for contexts requiring maximal pass rates, independent-resampling or LLM-guided iterative repair could produce higher yields at greater provider cost and governance complexity.

Statistical interpretation and limitations: The small number of discordant pairs (n = 1) makes the exact McNemar appropriate and yields p = 1.0; the paired-bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.015] quantifies uncertainty in the paired difference and excludes the preregistered 0.15 absolute-improvement target because the observed baseline was near-ceiling, reducing sensitivity. Threats to validity: internal validity is strong for the paired estimator and deterministic scoring; construct validity depends on emulator fidelity (control-plane dynamics like BGP convergence are not fully modeled); external validity is limited by one LLM model (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic curated bank focused on small changes; conclusion validity is limited by reduced discordant counts and the consequent low sensitivity to detect large absolute effects.

Reproducibility and auditability: All per-episode prompts/responses, provider-call traces, validator traces, the single deterministic repair trace, analysis scripts, paired contingency CSV, bootstrap parameters, and execution manifest are archived in the evidence bundle. Key artifact SHA-256s: execution/task_manifest.jsonl (eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0), analysis/condition_summary.csv (86ab6b56e3ec10aa54aa08480a8e1ef31b64d79bf22bc99dac1d8ed00628a68a), analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (aa1147b793eb71be336f715f6078a1d676ddbd9f7d10ca95bfe74fa4b5bfbf3d), and analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (59a3745f3504467e3433968928a83e63f73d4ea2f481cee294e7935221700055). These artifacts support auditors or replication studies to extract the repaired episode details (task_id, validator.violation_codes, repair_rule, before/after normalized_config).
sections.conclusion: We conducted an autonomy-locked, preregistered paired experiment to measure whether a bounded generate–verify–repair guard improves emulator-executable success for LLM-generated NetOps configurations under a shared-candidate generation budget. Ungated gpt-5-mini succeeded in 199/200; the deterministic guarded pipeline succeeded in 200/200. Observed paired difference = 0.005 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.015]). Under this estimand and task distribution the marginal yield of a conservative deterministic repair-on-same-candidate was negligible though auditable and low-cost. Deterministic validators remain valuable assurance gates. All artifacts required for independent audit, including the aggregate difficulty labels in execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256: eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a) and the per-episode repair traces, are archived in the study evidence bundle for immediate inspection and reanalysis.

disclosure_statement:
This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock defined by the initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human involvement prior to the lock: topic-family selection (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and master-prompt approval. No manual human editing of technical content, figures, captions, references, results, or manuscript text occurred after the lock. The autonomous pipeline performed literature search/verification, research-gap selection, preregistration (study_id cnd-001-5f3a), code generation, experiment execution, artifact capture, analysis, internal critique, peer-review checks, and manuscript drafting.

Models and tooling: generation requested gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json declared_model_version). Validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (syntactic parsing, structural/workflow checks, deterministic emulator application). Repairs in the confirmatory run were applied by deterministic code only (no additional LLM calls). Execution environment: Dockerized Mininet+FRR orchestrated by hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistered/enforced settings (not altered post-lock): primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sample n=200 paired intents; maximum model-call budget = 400; repair budget ≤1 deterministic repair iteration; primary analysis = exact McNemar two-sided (exact-binomial on discordant pairs); bootstrap CIs = 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729. Execution accounting (artifact-backed): completed 400 episodes with model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; repair-stage calls = 1). All prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, repair traces (single invoked repair trace), analysis artifacts, and execution manifest are archived in the study evidence bundle.
limitations: Synthetic, curated confirmatory task bank focused on small single- and small multi-device changes; not comprehensive of production NetOps workloads (multivendor CLI dialects, hardware idiosyncrasies, runtime control-plane timing).
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) evaluated; findings do not imply multi-model generality.
Deterministic emulator + validator model control-plane behavior but cannot fully capture real-world runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or device firmware idiosyncrasies.
Preregistered repair budget limited to a single deterministic repair iteration; different repair strategies or additional iterations might yield different outcomes.
Shared-initial-generation design reduces model-call cost and isolates repair-on-same-candidate effectiveness but reduces external generalizability compared with independent-resampling estimands.
Near-ceiling baseline success limited statistical power to analyze failure-mode distributions; exploratory failure-taxonomy conclusions are therefore constrained.
Adversarial or out-of-distribution intents (jailbreaks, malformed ambiguous intents) were not included in the confirmatory set and require separate evaluation.

Full per-task difficulty counts for all 200 confirmatory intents are recorded in execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a) in the archived evidence bundle; readers and auditors can extract exact counts and per-episode difficulty labels from that manifest.
